Try itRead \(u\): how far through the move a point \(s\) is
  • Pick a point \(s\) on the road, in meters along the right lane's center.
  • Candidate A: \(s_{0} = 60\) m, \(L = 40\) m.
  • \(u = (s - s_{0}) / L = (s - 60) / 40\): how far through the move that point is.
point \(s\)try it
\(s\) (m)\(u\)What it says
60(60 − 60) / 40 = 0the move starts: the AV is at \(s_{0}\)
70(70 − 60) / 40 = 0.25a quarter of the way through
80(80 − 60) / 40 = 0.5halfway through
100(100 − 60) / 40 = 1the move ends, at \(s_{0} + L\)
110(110 − 60) / 40 = 1.25past the end: the move is over
  • \(u\) has no unit: meters divided by meters. It is a share of the move.
  • Only 0 to 1 matters: past the end the AV stays at \(d_{0} + \Delta d\), so the code clips \(u\) to 1.
  • The same \(u\) works for every \(L\): halfway is \(u = 0.5\) for 20, 30 or 40 m.
